solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Where incumbent is changing one character who is spurned by others?

definitions.text: character who is spurned by others

indicators.note: asks for a single letter of the word to be swapped for another

parts.note: an incumbent is a vicar or rector, whose living is a parish

explanation.surface: A riddle about a clergyman whose post makes him an outsider shunned by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing one' swaps a single letter: the S of PARISH becomes A. 'character' does double duty in the surface as a letter, but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast whom society rejects and avoids is the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Soldiers guarding position may be unwelcome guests

indicators.note: the soldiers surround and protect the other word

parts.note: paras are paratroopers
a site is a location or position

explanation.surface: Troops guarding a post may not be wanted by their hosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spongers who live off a host without giving anything back are freeloaders.

clue.text: Reach weak animal with oxygen

parts.note: the runt is the smallest, weakest of a litter
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Getting to a sickly creature with an oxygen supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To amount to, as a bill runs to fifty pounds, is to reach a figure.

clue.text: Relieving everyone with wise words? That's not succeeded

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: the letter for 'succeeded' is to be absent

parts.note: a saying is a proverb, wise words
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Comforting everyone with wisdom, though without success.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing fears or pain is soothing or calming them, as in allaying doubts.

clue.text: Announcement of royal family's good news travelling fast across the globe?

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: the birth of a successor to the throne, an heir born

explanation.surface: News of a royal birth flashing around the world in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'travelling fast across the globe' seems to describe the news; it is the definition of flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flying through the air, like a plane crossing continents, is in flight and aloft.

clue.text: What the bridesmaid shows in island region

parts.note: what is shown in something lies in its inner part, so 'in' supplies the word for inside

indicators.note: the phrase shows only its central run of letters, the outer ones falling away

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid appearing in some Scottish island district.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the island name sits on the inside of 'the bridesmaid', so the phrase shows the inner part; bloggers called it a hidden word with a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: This archipelago off western Scotland includes Skye, Mull and Islay, forming a distinct island area.

clue.text: Lad collects brown plants growing in one area

indicators.note: the lad gathers the other word inside him

parts.note: a lad is a boy
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A boy gathers withered plants in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the science, the word means the flora or plant life of a particular region.

clue.text: After study chose to be up for election again

indicators.note: places the piece for 'chose' behind the one for 'study'

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
opted means chose

explanation.surface: Having thought about it, a politician decided to stand again.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate selected once more by the local party is standing for office a second time.

clue.text: Leave to dine, lover having gone earlier

indicators.note: puts the piece for the departed lover in front

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Permission to go out for dinner, now the boyfriend has left.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is formal permission for a pupil or student to be absent, a leave of absence.

clue.text: After row was first to get embittered

indicators.note: puts the piece for 'was first' behind the one for 'row'

parts.note: a rank is a row or line, as of soldiers or taxis
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Someone sours after a quarrel in which a rival came out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line, as in a taxi rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that rankled caused lasting resentment, the same as one that embittered someone.

clue.text: Dad's navigated at sea with the wind blowing in the wrong direction?

definitions.text: with the wind blowing in the wrong direction?

indicators.note: means all over the place, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Father sailing against a headwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad's' gives its S as a letter here: DADS plus NAVIGATED are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor facing a headwind is handicapped, held back by unfavourable conditions.

clue.text: Chemical element written about by class

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is set down backwards

parts.note: tin is a chemical element
rate as in first-rate, a class or grade

explanation.surface: A school class writing up a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chemical element' must be split: 'Chemical' alone is the definition and 'element' is TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate, a salt of nitric acid used in fertilisers, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Rumour beginning to sully politician

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Gossip starting to tarnish an MP's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A story can be an unconfirmed tale or report doing the rounds, i.e. gossip.

clue.text: Prolong call, not yielding over the course of it

indicators.note: one word stretches across the whole of another, holding it

parts.note: stout means staunch and unbending
to ring is to telephone, i.e. call

explanation.surface: Dragging out a phone conversation while refusing to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something out is to extend it in time, like an argument stretched for hours.

clue.text: Sad songs should be shortened, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are dressed up anew

explanation.surface: Someone thinks laments ought to be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reads as 'I think' but signals the shuffle of SHORTENED plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament or dirge for the dead, a mournful song.

clue.text: To square circle one would require jiggery-pokery!

indicators.note: jiggery-pokery is trickery or fiddling, so the letters must be fiddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Squaring the circle can only be done by cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is a verb here: to make two things agree.
explanation.definitionFit: To square accounts or differences is to make them agree or settle them.

clue.text: Like surgeon and assistants working at the highest level

definitions.meaning: a surgical team busy in theatre is at an operation

explanation.surface: A surgical team at the peak of their profession.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, AT OP: busy at an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on top of something, perched at the summit.

clue.text: Recorder of steps made by saint going round part of St Paul's

indicators.note: the saint encircles the other word

parts.note: St Peter the apostle
St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its dome

explanation.surface: A saint walking around St Paul's Cathedral counts his paces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer is a device that counts the walker's paces.

clue.text: One prisoner engaged in expressive sort of metalwork

indicators.note: the first pieces are fitted inside the word for 'expressive'

parts.note: free in the sense of unrestrained and open in expression
one is the Roman numeral I
an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A convict taking up an artistic kind of metal craft.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of the more usual FILIGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate ornamental tracery of fine gold or silver wire is a kind of jewellery work.

clue.text: Worker perhaps not at home in faction

indicators.note: says the letters for 'at home' are to be dropped

parts.note: a worker ant or bee is an example of an insect
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: An employee away from home involved in some group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker perhaps' is an insect, like a worker bee; 'perhaps' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a breakaway group within a larger religious or political body.

clue.text: Just as a gentleman is said to be by preference?

definitions.meaning: just as an adjective means fair and impartial

definitions.text: as a gentleman is said to be by preference?
definitions.meaning: gentlemen prefer blondes, so they are minded towards the fair-haired

explanation.surface: Just how a gentleman is supposed to prefer things.
explanation.walkthrough: Alludes to the film Gentlemen Prefer Blondes: inclined to fair hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impartial and unbiased is what it means to be just in judgement.

clue.text: Holy city's name in the papers etc

indicators.note: places the letter for 'name' within the other word

parts.note: newspapers and broadcasters together are the media

explanation.surface: A sacred city's name appearing in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Medina in Saudi Arabia, where the Prophet is buried, is Islam's second most sacred site.

clue.text: Trick broadcast? Person with final word gave permission

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
sent out over the airwaves, transmitted
the editor, abbreviated ED, decides what gets printed

explanation.surface: A deceptive broadcast is approved by whoever has the last say.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agreed or allowed something is to have assented to it.

clue.text: Silly saint going astray following around heathen god

indicators.note: the saint's letters wander off and another takes their place afterwards

parts.note: stupid means silly
c for circa means around

explanation.surface: A foolish saint wandering off after a pagan deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid was the Roman god of love, a pagan deity.

clue.text: A church celebration with wine brought round and tea

indicators.note: turned about, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: the Mass is the Eucharist, celebrated with bread and wine

explanation.surface: A church service with wine handed round, followed by a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea from the Indian state of that name.

clue.text: End of coal left in bag?

indicators.note: the letter for 'left' goes inside the bag

parts.note: a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: The last bit of coal left in the coal sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of coal' looks like an instruction to take a final letter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal dust and small fragments left at the bottom of the heap are a known term for the leftover fuel.

clue.text: Quietly publicising a parliamentary procedure

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
airing views means making them public

explanation.surface: Quietly making known some piece of Westminster business.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament, an MP from each side agree both to miss a vote so their absences cancel out.
explanation.definitionFit: This arrangement, matching absent MPs from opposing parties, is a standard Commons convention.

clue.text: Member of house staff gives alert -the old boy has passed away

indicators.note: says those letters are gone from the word

parts.note: watchful and observant
OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A butler raises the alarm because the elderly master has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic such as a maid or footman working in a household is a house employee.

clue.text: Uncompromising types, their dads, having no time for messing about

indicators.note: the remaining letters are fooled around with into a new order
tells us to take away the letter for 'time'

explanation.surface: Stubborn fathers who refuse to waste time on silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes T from THEIR, leaving HEIR; 'messing about' then rearranges HEIR plus DADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardliners who resist all change and never give ground are stubborn traditionalists.

clue.text: Spirits for someone barely touching food?

definitions.meaning: as in 'keep your ... up', meaning courage or morale
a person who just picks at a meal, like a bird nibbling

explanation.surface: Drink offered to a fussy eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep your pecker up' is a British idiom for stay cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, one's courage or cheerfulness is one's morale, as in the idiom about keeping it up.
